Chicken mince patties, on a "rice cake", with warm fennel and cauliflower salad, and sweet potato puree

Chicken Patties:
500gms chicken mince
3 basil leaves finely chopped
half a tsp of tumeric
1 egg shredded cheddar cheese (approx 1/4 cup) shredded parmesan cheese (approx 1/4 cup)
1 can diced tomatoes
a handful of spinace leaves - roughly chopped
paremsan cheese for the top

pre-heat oven to approx 150 celcius.

place mince, and all other ingredients, minus the tinned tomato and spinach, into a bowl, and mix together. heat a skillet with some oil (i used coconut), and spoon some chicken into the pan and flatten to desired thickness. sear it on each side, remove and place on a plate to cool for a bit.

in a baking dish, pour the tinned tomatoes in, and spread evenly across the bottom. evenly place the chicken patties into the baking dish, sprinkling the spinach and extra parmesan over the top. optional: add a few perino, or cherry, tomatoes, chopped in half. place the dish in the oven and cook for about 40 mins, or until the top looks nice and golden.

whilst the chicken is cooking, boil up some rice - approx. 1 cup. you'll need to make sure it's a little sticky so that it keeps it's shape should you choose to shape it. i used one of the kids sandwich boxes as the mould. once the rice is cooked, just spoon it in and flatten it until it looks like it's going to stay put.

with the sweet potato: i simply steamed a few slices of peeled and diced spud until it was soft. using a fork, and butter, i added and "smooshed" until it was smooth enough for my liking. optional: a pinch of powdered ginger to spice up the flavour of the potato.

the fennel and cauliflower was just chopped to desired volume, and steamed until tender.

i had a few baby truss tomatoes floating about the fridge, so i just placed them in the skillet on a low heat, and covered until the skin split a little.
Telling Kids To Dream Big Is A Big Con

July 19

20 Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen. - Matt 28:20 (KJV)

Jesus has been instructing His disciples to go into the entire world and teach the Gospel, and get people born again and made disciples. Jesus makes it clear that we are to make disciples (teaching) out of the people who accept Him, and not just converts. Most evangelistic efforts that get large numbers of people to confess Jesus as their Savior do not follow up and teach them the Word. That leaves a large number of people who believe they are saved, and yet don’t know what the commands of Jesus are. They must be taught to observe all things that Jesus has commanded, and not just be born again. As Jesus says, if you continue in my word, are you my disciples indeed (John 8:31). It is not enough to be born again and stuck.

If we are doing what Jesus commanded us to do, then He promises to be with us always, even to the end of the world. What did Jesus tell us to do? We are to love God above all, and love our neighbor as ourselves (Matthew 22:37-39), and we are to do the works that He did (John 14:12), as well as go into the whole world and teach the Gospel (Matthew 28:19). Before doing any of these things, you need to first make yourself a living sacrifice to God (Romans 12:1), and renew your mind with the Word of God (Romans 12:2). Do these things, and assure your salvation by living a life dedicated, out of love, to the Lord (Hebrews 5:9). Praise God for His goodness and mercy.

By: Pastor Joe W. Green www.Infinite-Faith.com
